about: This part ends the sixth day and begins the seventh. The forty-two deities who dawned at the end of the last part are described: neither large nor small, with their thrones and gestures, the five buddhas and their consorts in pairs, the bodhisattvas around them, the whole maṇḍala complete at once. Then from the hearts of the five families come the light-rays of the four wisdoms joined: on a strip of white light a white drop like a mirror turned face down, then a blue drop like a turquoise bowl, a yellow one like a golden bowl, and a red one like a bowl of coral. The green light of the fifth wisdom does not appear, because the dead man's awareness is not yet complete; the four together are called the path of the inner hollow of Vajrasattva. He is to remember his lama's instruction and know them again, as a child and its mother know each other when they meet. Beside them dawn the six dull lights of the six kinds of beings, which lead to rebirth, and he is to turn from them and say a prayer to the five families. The best, the middling and all the rest are freed so; most recognise the peaceful deities. But for the lowest, who had no tendency toward the teaching, the seventh day comes: the knowledge-holders come to meet them from the realm of the Sky-Goers, with the dull light of the animals, and the first of them dawns in a mass of rainbow light, the Lord of the Lotus Dance with his consort.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ སྐུ་ དེ་ དག་ ཀྱང་ མི་ ཆེ་བ༔ མི་ ཆུང་བ་ ཆ་མཉམ་པ༔ རྒྱན་ ཁ་དོག་ བཞུགས་ཚུལ་ དང་༔ གདན་ཁྲི་ རང་རང་ གི་ ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ དང་ བཅས་ཏེ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Bodies those (plural) also, not large, not small, proportion-even; ornaments, colours, sitting-manner and, seat-thrones, each-own's hand-seals with together, and:
sentences.i: O child of noble family, these forms are neither large nor small but evenly proportioned, each with its own ornaments, colour, manner of sitting, throne and hand-gesture.
sentences.n: The sentence that the last part left for p. 63: it describes the forty-two deities just named. mi che ba mi chung ba, 'not large, not small'; cha mnyam pa, 'even in proportion' (cha, 'part, proportion'; mnyam pa, 'equal'). bzhugs tshul, 'manner of sitting' (bzhugs, the respectful 'sit'; tshul, 'manner'). gdan khri, 'seat and throne'. rang rang gi, 'each its own', rang doubled. phyag rgya, 'hand-seal' (Sanskrit mudrā), the gesture of the hands. dang bcas te, 'together with, and': the sentence runs on. de dag, 'those', the plural, as in 006. The other recension adds cha lugs, 'dress', after rgyan, 'ornaments'.

sentences.w: སྐུ་ དེ་ དག་ ཀྱང་ ལྔ་ལྔའི་ ཟུང་ གིས་ ཁྱབ་པ༔ ལྔ་ཚན་ རེ་རེ་ ལ་ འོད་ ལྔའི་ ཚོམ་བུས་ མུ་ཁྱུད་ དང་ བཅས་པ༔
sentences.l: Bodies those (plural) also, five-five's pairs by pervaded; five-groups each to, lights five's clusters-by rim with together,
sentences.i: These forms come in pairs, five and five, filling the whole space, and each group of five has a rim of clustered lights of five colours:
sentences.n: lnga lnga'i zung, 'pairs of five and five': taken as the five buddhas, each with his consort, and so the five pairs; the words are short, and the sense is not sure. khyab pa, 'pervaded, filled through'; the other recension has brgyan pa, 'adorned', 'adorned by the pairs'. lnga tshan, 'a set of five' (tshan, 'group'); re re la, 'to each one'. tshom bus, 'by clusters' (tshom bu, 'cluster, bunch', with -s, 'by'): the rim is made of clusters of light. mu khyud, 'rim, border, enclosing ring'. The other recension has 'od lnga'i mu khyud, 'a rim of five lights', without the clusters.

sentences.w: ཡབ་ ཀྱི་ ཆ་ འཛིན་པའི་ རིགས་ ཀྱི་ སེམས་དཔའ་ དང༔ ཡུམ་ གྱི་ ཆ་ འཛིན་པའི་ རིགས་ ཀྱི་ སེམས་མ་ དང་༔ དཀྱིལ་འཁོར་ ཐམས་ཅད་ གཅིག་ ལ་ རྫོགས་པར་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་བས༔ དེ་ ཁྱོད་ ཀྱི་ ཡི་དམ་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ ཡིན་བས་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: the father's part holding's family's heroes and; the mother's part holding's family's heroines and: maṇḍala all one-in complete-way dawning comes-because: that, your yidam's deity it-is-because, face-knowing do!
sentences.i: the bodhisattvas of the families, who take the father's part, and the female bodhisattvas of the families, who take the mother's part: the whole maṇḍala dawns, complete in one. That is your yidam deity: recognise it.
sentences.n: cha 'dzin pa, 'holding the part (of)': in each family the bodhisattvas (sems dpa') stand on the father's side and the female bodhisattvas (sems ma) on the mother's. dkyil 'khor, 'maṇḍala', the circle of a deity and his retinue. gcig la rdzogs par, 'complete in one'; the other recension has dus gcig la, 'at one time'. rdzogs is not sure on the image: the letter under the r may be j, which would give rjogs, no word; rdzogs, which the sense needs and the other recension has, is read. Its last letters are cut as one sign for -gs, here written out. 'ong bas, 'because it comes', runs on to the command (the other recension ends the sentence with 'ong ngo). yin bas, 'because it is', is the print's b for p (yin pas), as in 006. yi dam, the deity a person takes as his own in practice.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ རིགས་ལྔ་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ དེ་ དག་ གི་ ཐུགས་ཀ་ ནས༔ ཡེ་ཤེས་ བཞི་ སྦྱོར་ གྱི་ འོད་ཟེར་ ཕྲ་ ལ་ དྭངས་པ༔ ཉི་མའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ སྦ་ཐག་ དྲིལ་བ་ ལྟ་བུ་ མེ་རེ་རེ་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ སྙིང་ཁར་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Five-families father-mother those (plural)'s heart from, wisdoms four joined's light-rays, fine and clear, sun's light-rays cane-cord twisted like, shimmering(?), you-yourself's heart-at dawning come, and:
sentences.i: O child of noble family, from the heart of the five families, the buddhas and their consorts, the light-rays of the four wisdoms joined, fine and clear, come dawning at your heart, shimmering like rays of the sun twisted into a cord.
sentences.n: ye shes bzhi sbyor, 'the four wisdoms joined', the vision named at the end of the last part. phra la dwangs pa, 'fine and clear': la between two adjectives is 'and'. sba thag, 'a cord of cane' (sba, 'cane'; thag, 'rope, cord'), and dril ba, 'wound, twisted': the thin rays come wound together like a cord; the other recension has ba thag sbrel ba, 'joined like a rope', and the likeness is not sure in either. The print has me re re, plainly on the image; the other recension has only re re, 'one by one', and does not have me. me re re is taken here as the word of 003, a doubled-sound word for a flickering shimmer; it may also be that me does not belong and re re is 'each', 'each comes to your heart'. Which, cannot be told; the reading is uncertain. snying khar, 'at the heart'. 'char du 'ong ste, 'come to dawn, and': the sentence runs on into the four lights, one by one.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ དང་པོ་ རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ ཀྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀ་ ནས༔ ཆོས་ཀྱི་དབྱིངས་ ཀྱི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ དཀར་ ལ་ གསལ་བ༔ བཀྲག་ ལ་ ཉམ་ང་བའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ གྱི་ སྣམ་བུ་ ཅིག༔ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ སྙིང་ཁ་ དང་ འབྲེལ་མར་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: That moreover: first, Vairocana's heart from, dharma-expanse's wisdom, white and bright, lustrous and fearsome's light-ray's strip, one, you-yourself's heart with joined-way dawning comes.
sentences.i: First, from the heart of Vairocana, a strip of light-rays of the wisdom of the expanse of reality, white and bright, lustrous and fearsome, comes dawning, joined to your heart.
sentences.n: de yang, 'and that, namely': it opens the account of the four lights. dang po, 'first'; the other recension dang por. chos kyi dbyings kyi ye shes, 'the wisdom of the expanse of reality', Vairocana's (004). nyam nga ba, 'fearsome', here in its usual spelling, where 003 and 006 printed nyams nga ba. snam bu, 'a strip of woollen cloth': a band of light. cig, 'one', makes it 'a strip'. 'brel mar, 'joined, connected' ('brel, 'be connected', with mar, as in gshibs mar, 'side by side').

sentences.w: འོད་ཟེར་ གྱི་ སྣམ་བུ་ དེའི་ སྟེང་དུ་ ཐིག་ལེ་ དཀར་པོ་ འོད་ཟེར་ དང་ ལྡན་པ་ མེ་ལོང་ ཁ་སྦུབ་པ་ ཙམ་པ༔ ཤིན་ཏུ་ གསལ་བ་ བཀྲག་ ལ་ འཚེར་བ༔
sentences.l: Light-ray's strip that's on-top-at, drop white, light-rays with endowed, mirror mouth-down about-size, very bright, lustrous and shimmering,
sentences.i: On that strip of light there is a white drop, giving out rays, about the size of a mirror turned face down, very bright, lustrous and shimmering,
sentences.n: steng du, 'on top of, on'; the other recension has nang du, 'within'. thig le, 'drop, sphere', as in the last parts. kha sbub pa, 'turned mouth-down' (kha, 'mouth, face'; sbub, 'turned over'): a round mirror laid face down, so that its back rises like a dome. tsam pa, 'about the size of' (tsam, 'as much as'). The sentence runs on.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ རང་བཞིན་ གྱི་ ཐིག་ལེ་ ལྔ་ལྔས་ བརྒྱན་པ༔ དེའི་ མཐའ་ དང་ དབུས་ མེད་པར་ ཐིག་ལེ་ དང་ ཐིག་ཕྲན་ གྱིས་ བརྒྱན་པ་ ཅིག་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: That moreover, nature's drops five-five-by adorned; its edge and centre without-way, drops and small-drops by adorned, one, dawning comes.
sentences.i: it is adorned in turn with drops of its own nature, five by five, and, with no edge or centre, adorned with drops and smaller drops: so it comes to dawn.
sentences.n: rang bzhin gyi thig le, 'drops of its own nature, natural drops'. lnga lngas, 'by fives' (lnga, 'five', doubled, with -s, 'by'). de'i mtha' dang dbus med par, 'without its edge or centre': the drops fill it everywhere. thig phran, 'small drop'. brgyan pa, 'adorned', the past of rgyan. cig, 'one', makes it 'a drop'; the other recension has no cig.

sentences.w: རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའི་ ཐུགས་ཀ་ ནས༔ མེ་ལོང་ ལྟ་བུའི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ མཐིང་ ལ་ གསལ་བའི་ སྣམ་བུའི་ སྟེང་དུ༔ ཐིག་ལེ་ སྔོན་པོ་ འོད་ དང་ ལྡན་པ་ དཔེར་ན་ གཡུའི་ ཕོར་པ་ ཁ་སྦུབ་པ་ ཙམ་པ༔ ཐིག་ལེ་ དང་ ཐིག་ཕྲན་ གྱིས་ བརྒྱན་པ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Vajrasattva's heart from, mirror like's wisdom, blue and bright's strip's on-top-at, drop blue, light with endowed, for-example turquoise's bowl mouth-down about-size, drops and small-drops by adorned, dawning comes.
sentences.i: From the heart of Vajrasattva, on a strip of the mirror-like wisdom, blue and bright, a blue drop full of light comes dawning, the size of a turquoise bowl turned upside down, adorned with drops and smaller drops.
sentences.n: me long lta bu'i ye shes, 'the mirror-like wisdom', Vajrasattva's (004). mthing, 'deep blue, azure'; sngon po, 'blue'. dper na, 'for example, as it were'. g.yu, 'turquoise'; phor pa, 'bowl, cup' (the usual spelling phor ba; the print writes pa each time). The other recension has thig le mthing ka g.yu'i phor ba, 'a deep-blue drop, a turquoise bowl', without 'od dang ldan pa, 'full of light', and dper na.

sentences.w: རིན་ཆེན་འབྱུང་ལྡན་ གྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀ་ ནས༔ མཉམ་པ་ཉིད་ ཀྱི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ སེར་ ལ་ གསལ་བའི་ སྣམ་བུའི་ སྟེང་དུ༔ ཐིག་ལེ་ སེར་པོ་ གསེར་ གྱི་ ཕོར་པ་ ཁ་སྦུབ་པ་ ལྟ་བུ༔ ཐིག་ལེ་ དང་ ཐིག་ཕྲན་ གྱིས་ བརྒྱན་པ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Ratnasambhava's heart from, sameness's wisdom, yellow and bright's strip's on-top-at, drop yellow, gold's bowl mouth-down like, drops and small-drops by adorned, dawning comes.
sentences.i: From the heart of Ratnasambhava, on a strip of the wisdom of sameness, yellow and bright, a yellow drop comes dawning like a golden bowl turned upside down, adorned with drops and smaller drops.
sentences.n: mnyam pa nyid kyi ye shes, 'the wisdom of sameness', Ratnasambhava's (005). ser, 'yellow'; gser, 'gold'. lta bu, 'like', where the blue drop had tsam pa, 'the size of'.

sentences.w: སྣང་བ་མཐའ་ཡས་ ཀྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀ་ ནས༔ སོ་སོར་ རྟོགས་པའི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ དམར་ ལ་ གསལ་བའི་ སྣམ་བུའི་ སྟེང་དུ༔ ཐིག་ལེ་ དམར་པོ་ འོད་ཟེར་ དང་ ལྡན་པ་ དཔེར་ན་ བྱུ་རུའི་ ཕོར་པ་ ཁ་སྦུབ་པ་ ལྟ་བུ༔ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ མདངས་ དང་ ལྡན་པ་ ཤིན་ཏུ་ གསལ་ ལ་ མཚེར་བ༔
sentences.l: Amitābha's heart from, discerning's wisdom, red and bright's strip's on-top-at, drop red, light-rays with endowed, for-example coral's bowl mouth-down like, wisdom's radiance with endowed, very bright and shimmering,
sentences.i: From the heart of Amitābha, on a strip of the discerning wisdom, red and bright, a red drop full of rays, like a coral bowl turned upside down, with the radiance of wisdom, very bright and shimmering,
sentences.n: so sor rtogs pa'i ye shes, 'the discerning wisdom', Amitābha's (005). byu ru, 'coral'; the other recension byi ru. mdangs, 'radiance, glow'; the other recension has gting mdangs, 'deep radiance'. mtsher ba is read as 'tsher ba, 'shimmering', as in 006; the print wrote 'tsher ba of the white drop above. The sentence runs on.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ ཐིག་ལེ་ ལྔ་ལྔས་ བརྒྱན་པ༔ དེའི་ མཐའ་ དང་ དབུས་ མེད་པར་ ཐིག་ལེ་ དང་ ཐིག་ཕྲན་ གྱིས་ བརྒྱན་པ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: That moreover, drops five-five-by adorned; its edge and centre without-way, drops and small-drops by adorned, dawning comes.
sentences.i: it is adorned in turn with drops, five by five, and, with no edge or centre, adorned with drops and smaller drops: so it comes to dawn.
sentences.n: The words of the white drop, without rang bzhin gyi, 'of its own nature' (the other recension has rang bzhin gyis here).

sentences.w: དེ་ རྣམས་ ཀྱང་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ སྙིང་ཁ་ དང་ འབྲེལ་ ནས་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Those (plural) also, you-yourself's heart with joined, then, dawning come.
sentences.i: These too come dawning, joined to your heart.
sentences.n: 'brel nas, 'joined, then', where the first had 'brel mar; the other recension has 'brel mar here too. Four lights, not five: why the green is missing is said below.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ དེ་ རྣམས་ ཀྱང་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ རིག་པའི་ རང་རྩལ་ ལས་ འཆར་བ་ ཡིན་ ཏེ༔ གཞན་ ཞིག་ ནས་ འོངས་པ་ མ་ ཡིན་པས༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Those (plural) also, you-yourself's knowing's own-energy from dawning it-is, and: another somewhere from came are-not-because:
sentences.i: O child of noble family, these too dawn out of the natural energy of your own awareness, and have not come from anywhere else. So
sentences.n: rang rtsal, 'own energy, natural play', as in 006. gzhan zhig nas, 'from somewhere else'. 'ongs pa, 'having come', the past stem of 'ong; ma yin pas, 'because it is not', runs on to the commands. The other recension has shar ba, 'dawned', for 'char ba, and 'ong ba for 'ongs pa.

sentences.w: དེ་ རྣམས་ ལ་ ཆགས་པར་ ཡང་ མ་ བྱེད་ཅིག༔ སྐྲག་པར་ ཡང་ མ་ བྱེད་ཅིག་ མི་ རྟོག་བའི་ ངང་དུ་ ཀློད་ ལ་ ཞོག་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Those (plural) to attached-way also not do! Afraid-way also not do! Not-conceiving's state-in relax, and, rest!
sentences.i: do not be attached to them, and do not be afraid of them either: relax and rest in a state free of concepts.
sentences.n: ma … cig with the present stem byed makes a prohibition, as before; yang, 'also, either'. The print has no ༔ after the second cig. mi rtog ba'i ngang, 'the state of not conceiving' (rtog pa, 'to think, to build concepts'), with the print's b for p: the mind resting without making thoughts of what appears; the other recension has rnam par mi rtog pa'i ngang. klod, 'relax, let loose', the word the other recension wrote in 006, where the print had glod; here the other recension has lhod, of the same sense. zhog, the imperative of 'jog, 'to put, to leave'.

sentences.w: དེའི་ ངང་ ལ་ སྐུ་ དང་ འོད་ཟེར་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ཁྱོད་རང་ ལ་ ཐིམ་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: That's state-in, bodies and light-rays all you-yourself into dissolving, then, buddha become.
sentences.i: In that state all the forms and light-rays will dissolve into you, and you will become a buddha.
sentences.n: The print writes thams cad with the small circle above the line (ཐཾས) for the m of thams, a contraction, here written out. thim, 'to dissolve, to melt into'. sangs rgyas par 'gyur ro, 'will become a buddha', as in 006.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ བྱ་བ་ གྲུབ་པའི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ ལྗང་ཁུ་ ནི་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ རིག་པའི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ རང་རྩལ་ མ་ རྫོགས་པས་ མི་ སྣང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Deeds accomplished's wisdom's light green, as-for, you-yourself's knowing's wisdom's own-energy not complete-because, not appears.
sentences.i: O child of noble family, the green light of the wisdom that accomplishes deeds does not appear, because the natural energy of the wisdom of your awareness is not yet complete.
sentences.n: Why there are four lights and not five: the green light of Amoghasiddhi's wisdom (006) is missing. ni sets it as the topic, 'as for the green light'. ma rdzogs pas, 'because it is not complete'. mi snang ngo, 'does not appear', with mi, the 'not' of the present, and the sentence-ending -ngo.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ དེ་ རྣམས་ ཀྱི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ བཞི་ སྦྱོར་ གྱི་ སྣང་བ་ ཞེས་ བྱ་ སྟེ༔ རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའ་ ཁོང་གསེང་ གི་ ལམ་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Those (plural)-of(?): wisdoms four joined's appearance so-called, and: Vajrasattva inner-hollow's path so-called it-is.
sentences.i: O child of noble family, these are called the vision of the four wisdoms joined; that is what is called the path of the inner hollow of Vajrasattva.
sentences.n: de rnams kyi has kyi, 'of', where the other recension has ni, 'as for': 'these are what is called'; the print's kyi is read so. zhes bya ste, 'is called, and'. khong gseng, 'the hollow within, the inner passage' (khong, 'inside'; gseng, 'gap, opening'); the usual spelling is khong seng, which the print itself has a few lines below and the other recension has in both places. The text does not explain the name: the four lights, joined, are a path by which one passes into Vajrasattva. rdo rje sems dpa' stands here without -'i, 'of'; the other recension has rdo rje sems dpa'i.

sentences.w: དེའི་ ཚེ་ ཁྱོད་ ཀྱིས་ སྔར་ བླ་མས་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པའི་ གདམས་ངག་ དྲན་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That's time, by-you, before, by-the-lama face-introduced's instruction remembering do!
sentences.i: At that time call to mind the instruction by which your lama pointed this out to you before.
sentences.n: Two doers in one sentence: khyod kyis, 'by you', the one who is to remember, and bla mas, 'by the lama', the one who pointed it out. gdams ngag, 'instruction', a lama's oral advice (002). dran par gyis shig, 'remember!' (dran pa, 'to remember', with -r, and gyis shig, 'do!').

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་ ཀྱི་ ངོ་སྤྲད་ དེ་ དྲན་ ན་ སྔར་ ཤར་བའི་ སྣང་བ་ དེ་ རྣམས་ ལ་ ཡིད་ཆེས་ ནས་ མ་ དང་ བུ་ འཕྲད་པ་ ལྟ་བུའམ༔ སྔར་ འདྲིས་པའི་ མི་ ཕྱིས་ མཐོང་བ་ ཙམ་ གྱིས་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ སྒྲོ་འདོགས་ ཆོད་པ་ ལྟ་བུ༔
sentences.l: Your face-introduction that remember if, before dawned's appearances those (plural) in trust having, then: mother and child meeting like-or, before familiar's person later seeing merely by, face-know, doubt cut, like:
sentences.i: If you remember that pointing-out of yours, you will trust the visions that dawned before. It will be like a mother and child meeting, or like seeing again someone you knew well: at the mere sight you recognise him, and all doubt is cut.
sentences.n: khyod kyi ngo sprad, 'your pointing-out', the one given to you; the other recension has khyod kyis ngo sprod kyi don dran na, 'if you remember the meaning of the pointing-out'. shar ba'i, 'that dawned', shar, the past stem of 'char. yid ches, 'to trust, to believe' (yid, 'mind'; ches, 'believe'). Two likenesses, the first closed by -'am, 'or', written onto lta bu, 'like', as on mal sa in the pilot. ma dang bu 'phrad pa, 'mother and child meeting'. 'dris pa'i mi, 'a person one has been familiar with'; phyis, 'later'; mthong ba tsam gyis, 'by merely seeing'. sgro 'dogs, 'superimposition, doubt' (sgro, 'feather'; 'dogs, 'tie'): what the mind adds to what is there; chod pa, 'cut'.

sentences.w: རང་སྣང་དུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པས་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ རྣམ་པར་ དག་པའི་ ལམ་ འགྱུར་བ་ མེད་པར་ ཡིད་ཆེས་ ནས༔ རྒྱུན་ གྱི་ ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ སྐྱེས་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: As-self-appearance face-knowing-because, reality-itself completely pure's path, change without-way, trust having, then, continuity's absorption arose, and:
sentences.i: Recognising them as your own appearance, you will trust without wavering in the path of reality, wholly pure; an unbroken absorption will arise,
sentences.n: rang snang du ngo shes pas, 'because you recognise them as your own appearance', the words of 003 and 006. 'gyur ba med par, 'without change': taken with yid ches, 'trust unwaveringly'; the other recension has lam 'gyur ba med pa yin par yid ches, 'trust that it is the unchanging path'. rgyun gyi ting nge 'dzin, 'an absorption of continuity': meditative absorption (samādhi) that does not break. skyes, the past stem of skye, 'to arise', with te, 'and'.

sentences.w: རིག་པ་ ལྷུན་གྲུབ་ ཆེན་པོའི་ སྐུ་ ལ་ ཐིམ་ ནས་ ལོངས་སྤྱོད་རྫོགས་པའི་སྐུར་ སངས་རྒྱས་ ཏེ་ ཕྱིར་ མི་ ལྡོག་གོ༔
sentences.l: Knowing spontaneous-presence great's body into dissolving, then, as-the-body-of-perfect-enjoyment buddha-become, and: back not turn.
sentences.i: Awareness will dissolve into the body of great spontaneous presence, and you will become a buddha in the body of perfect enjoyment, never to turn back.
sentences.n: lhun grub chen po, 'great spontaneous presence', a short form of lhun gyis grub pa (006). longs spyod rdzogs pa'i skur, 'as the body of perfect enjoyment', as in 006. phyir mi ldog go, 'does not turn back' (phyir, 'back'; ldog, 'turn'; -go, the sentence-ending after -g): the state of one who will not fall back into saṃsāra.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ དང་ མཉམ་དུ་ མ་ དག་ འཁྲུལ་བའི་ སྣང་བ་ རིགས་དྲུག་ གི་ འོད་ དྲུག་ ཀྱང་ གཅིག་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ ཏེ༔ གང་ ཞེ་ ན༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Wisdom's light with together, impure delusion's appearances, six-kinds' lights six also, as-one(?) dawning come, and: which, if-one-says:
sentences.i: O child of noble family, together with the light of wisdom the six lights of the six kinds of beings, the impure appearances of delusion, will also dawn all together. Which are they?
sentences.n: ma dag 'khrul ba'i snang ba, 'the impure appearances of delusion'. rigs drug, 'the six kinds', the six realms of rebirth, whose dull lights came one at a time beside the wisdom lights of the days before. gcig, 'one', is taken as 'together, at once', as dus gcig la, 'at one time', in 006; the sense is not sure. The other recension has rigs drug gi 'od 'char du 'ong ste, without drug kyang and gcig. gang zhe na, 'if one asks which', with zhe, the form zhes takes before na: the way a list is opened.

sentences.w: ལྷའི་ འོད་ དཀར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དང་༔ ལྷ་མ་ཡིན་ གྱི་ འོད་ དམར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དང་༔ མིའི་ འོད་ སྔོན་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དང་༔ དུད་འགྲོའི་ འོད་ ལྗང་ཁུ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དང་༔ ཡི་དྭགས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ སེར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དང་༔ དམྱལ་པའི་ འོད་ དུ་ཁ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དང༔ དག་པ་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ དང་ གཤིབས་མར་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང༔
sentences.l: The gods' light, white, lustreless, and; the demigods' light, red, lustreless, and; humans' light, blue, lustreless, and; animals' light, green, lustreless, and; hungry-ghosts' light, yellow, lustreless, and; hell's light, smoky, lustreless, and: pure wisdom's light with side-by-side dawning come.
sentences.i: The dull white light of the gods, the dull red light of the demigods, the dull blue light of humans, the dull green light of animals, the dull yellow light of the hungry ghosts and the dull smoky light of the hells: these dawn side by side with the light of pure wisdom.
sentences.n: dud 'gro, 'animal', the common word, where 006 had byol song. dmyal pa'i, 'of hell', where 004 and the other recension have dmyal ba'i. du kha is read, as in 004, as dud kha, 'smoke-coloured': the print writes du kha, here as there, and the other recension has dud ka; du kha by itself gives no sense, so the reading is uncertain. gshibs mar, 'side by side'. The sentence ends with 'ong, without the closing -ngo (the other recension 'ong ngo).

sentences.w: དེ་ཙ་ན་ ཁྱོད་ གང་ ལ་ ཡང་ འཛིན་པ་ དང་༔ ཆགས་པ་ མ་ བྱེད་པར༔ དམིགས་པ་ མེད་པའི་ ངང་ ལ་ ཀློད་ ལ་ ཞོག་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: At-that-time, you, whatever to even, grasping and attachment not doing-way, reference without's state-in relax, and, rest!
sentences.i: At that time do not grasp at any of them or cling to them, but relax and rest in the state that has no object.
sentences.n: gang la yang, 'to anything at all'. 'dzin pa, 'grasping, holding': the mind taking hold of what it sees. ma byed par, 'without doing'; the other recension has ma byed cig, 'do not!', and ends the sentence there. dmigs pa med pa'i ngang, 'the state without reference': dmigs pa is the object the mind fixes on; the other recension has mi dmigs pa'i ngang. klod and zhog cig as above.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་ དག་པ་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ ལ་ སྐྲག་ ཅིང་༔ མ་ དག་ རིགས་དྲུག་ འཁོར་བའི་ འོད་ ལ་ ཆགས་ ན་ ནི༔ འགྲོ་བ་ རིགས་དྲུག་ གི་ ལུས་ བླངས་ ཏེ༔ འཁོར་བ་ སྡུག་བསྔལ་ གྱི་ རྒྱ་མཚོ་ ཆེན་པོ་ ནས་ ཐར་པའི་ དུས་ མེད་བས་ འོ་རྒྱལ་ལོ༔
sentences.l: You, pure wisdom's light at afraid, and, impure six-kinds saṃsāra's light to attached if, as-for: beings six-kinds' body taken, and: saṃsāra suffering's ocean great from, liberation's time there-is-not-because, alas-weary!
sentences.i: If you are afraid of the light of pure wisdom and attached to the impure light of saṃsāra, the light of the six kinds, you will take a body among the six kinds of beings, and there will be no time when you are freed from the great ocean of suffering that is saṃsāra. How wearisome!
sentences.n: chags na ni, 'if attached, then'. 'gro ba, 'beings, those who go'. blangs, the past stem of len, 'to take': lus blangs, 'taken a body', that is, born. thar pa'i dus, 'the time of liberation'. med bas, 'because there is not', with the print's b for p (med pas); the letter is not sure on the image, where it looks more like ', which gives no word: bas, which the transcription of this print has, is read, and the other recension has pas; the sense is the same either way. 'o rgyal lo, 'how wearisome!', a cry of weariness: 003 had 'o brgyal, with b, of the dead man worn out, and the other recension has 'o brgyal lo here. The print writes rgyal lo as one syllable (རྒྱལོ), a contraction written out here.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ཁྱོད་ བླ་མའི་ གདམས་ངག་ ངོ་སྤྲོད་ མེད་པ་ ཅིག་ ཡིན་ ན་ ནི༔ གོང་ གི་ སྐུ་ དང་ དག་པ་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ ལ་ འཛིགས་ ཤིང་ སྐྲག་ ནས༔ མ་ དག་ འཁོར་བའི་ འོད་ ལ་ ཆགས་སུ་ འོང་བས༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! You, lama's instruction, face-introduction, without, one, are if, as-for: above's bodies and pure wisdom's light at afraid and, terrified, then, impure saṃsāra's light to attached coming-because:
sentences.i: O child of noble family, if you are someone without the lama's instruction, the pointing-out, you will fear and dread the forms described above and the light of pure wisdom, and come to cling to the impure light of saṃsāra. So
sentences.n: bla ma'i gdams ngag ngo sprod, 'the lama's instruction, the pointing-out', two nouns side by side; the other recension has gdam ngag gi ngo sprod, 'the pointing-out of the instruction'. med pa cig yin na, 'if you are one without'. gong gi sku, 'the forms above', those just described. 'dzigs is the print's spelling of 'jigs, 'to fear', which the other recension has; 'jigs shing skrag, two words of fear joined by shing, 'and'. chags su 'ong bas, 'because you come to be attached', as bros su 'ong, 'come fleeing', in 006; the other recension has chags tu.

sentences.w: དེ་ལྟར་ མ་ བྱེད་པར་ དག་པ་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ བཀྲག་ ལ་ འཚེར་བ་ དེ་ རྣམས་ ལ་ མོས་གུས་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Thus not doing-way, pure wisdom's lights, lustrous and shimmering, those (plural) to devotion-respect do!
sentences.i: Do not act so: turn with devotion and respect to those lights of pure wisdom, lustrous and shimmering.
sentences.n: de ltar ma byed par, 'not doing so'. mos gus gyis shig, 'do devotion!', as in 005.

sentences.w: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རིགས་ལྔ་ བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་པའི་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཀྱི་ འོད་ཟེར་ གྱིས་ བདག་ ལ་ ཐུགས་རྗེས་ འཛིན་པ་ ལ་ བྱོན་པར་ འདུག་ གིས་ སྐྱབས་སུ་ མཆིའོ་ སྙམ་པའི་ མོས་པ་ གྱིས་ ལ༔
sentences.l: 'The Blessed-Ones five-families Sugatas' compassion's wisdom's light-rays by, me to, compassion-by holding for come is, so; for-refuge I-go' thinking's devotion do, and,
sentences.i: Turn with devotion, thinking, 'The light-rays of the compassionate wisdom of the Blessed Ones, the Sugatas of the five families, have come to take hold of me with compassion: I go to them for refuge.'
sentences.n: The refuge formula of the days before, now for all five families at once. bde bar gshegs pa, 'one gone to bliss' (Sanskrit sugata), a name of a buddha. 'od zer gyis, 'by the light-rays', marks them as those who come. thugs rjes 'dzin pa, 'to hold with compassion' (thugs rje, 'compassion', with -s, 'by'): the hook of compassion of the days before. byon, the respectful verb 'to come', with one form for every tense. byon par 'dug gis, 'have come, and so': 'dug after a verb, as in 002 (bab nas 'dug gis), with gis, 'and so'. The other recension has 'od zer without gyis, 'byon par 'dug gi, and mos pa mdzod la, with the respectful 'do', where the print has gyis la.

sentences.w: འཁྲུལ་པ་ རིགས་དྲུག་ གི་ འོད་ ལ་ མ་ ཆགས་ མ་ ཞེན་པར༔ སངས་རྒྱས་ རིགས་ལྔ་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ ལ་ མདུན་པ་ རྩེ་གཅིག་ཏུ་ གཏོད་ ལ༔ སྨོན་ལམ་ འདི་སྐད་དུ་ ཐོབ་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: Delusion six-kinds' lights to not attached, not clinging-way, buddhas five-families father-mother to longing(?) one-pointedly direct, and: prayer these-words-in obtain(?)!
sentences.i: Without attachment or clinging to the deluded lights of the six kinds, direct a single-minded longing to the buddhas of the five families and their consorts, and make this prayer:
sentences.n: As on the days before (006). 'khrul pa, 'delusion, deluded'. ma chags ma zhen par, 'not attached, not clinging'. mdun pa is read, as in 003, as 'dun pa, 'longing, aspiration', which the other recension has here and the print itself had in 006; mdun pa is 'front', and 'turn your front one-pointedly toward' is possible but less likely. smon lam 'di skad du thob cig, read, as before, as a guess, 'make this prayer'.

sentences.w: ཀྱེ་མ་ དུག་ ལྔ་ དྲག་པོས་ འཁོར་བར་ འཁྱམས་པའི་ ཚེ༔ / ཡེ་ཤེས་ བཞི་ སྦྱོར་ གསལ་བའི་ འོད་ལམ་ ལ༔ / བཅོམ་ལྡན་ རྒྱལ་བ་ རིགས་ལྔས་ ལམ་སྣ་ དྲོངས༔ / དབྱིངས་ ཀྱི་ ཡུམ་ཆེན་ ལྔ་ ཡིས་ རྒྱབ་ ནས་ སྐྱོར༔ / མ་ དག་ རིགས་དྲུག་ འོད་ལམ་ བསྒྲལ་དུ་ གསོལ༔ / བར་དོ་ འཇིགས་པའི་ འཕྲང་ ལས་ བསྒྲལ་ ནས་ ཀྱང༔ / དག་པའི་ ཞིང་ མཆོག་ ལྔ་རུ་ བསྐྱལ་དུ་ གསོལ༔
sentences.l:
Alas! Poisons five fierce-by in-saṃsāra wandering's time,
wisdoms four joined bright's light-path on,
the Blessed victors five-families-by the-way lead!
Expanse's great-mothers five by from-behind support!
Impure six-kinds light-paths freeing I-pray;
the between fearful's narrow-passage from having-freed, also,
pure's realms supreme five-to bringing I-pray!
sentences.i:
Alas! When I wander in saṃsāra through the five fierce poisons,
on the bright light-path of the four wisdoms joined
may the Blessed Victors of the five families lead the way,
may the five great mothers of the expanse support me from behind.
I pray you, free me from the impure light-paths of the six kinds,
and when you have freed me from the fearful narrow passage of the bardo,
I pray you, bring me to the five supreme pure realms.
sentences.n: The prayer of the days before, now for the five families together, nine syllables to the line after kye ma, and seven lines where the days before had six. kye ma is the print's other spelling of kyai ma, used beside it. dug lnga, 'the five poisons', the poisons of the five days: delusion, anger, pride, desire and jealousy. rgyal ba, 'victor', a name of a buddha; rigs lngas, 'by the five families', with -s, 'by'. dbyings kyi yum chen, 'the great mothers of the expanse', the five consorts; yis, 'by', after a vowel; the other recension has yum mchog rigs lnga'i yum gyis, 'by the supreme mothers, the mothers of the five families'. skyor, 'hold up!', the present and imperative stem, as on the first and fifth days. The fifth line has no las, 'from': ma dag rigs drug 'od lam bsgral du gsol is read as 'free me from the impure light-paths of the six kinds', the sense the next line gives with las; the other recension has bar do rigs drug 'od lam, 'the light-paths of the six kinds in the bardo'. bsgral, the future stem of sgrol, 'to free', and bskyal, the past and future stem of skyel, 'to bring' (skyel / bskyal / bskyal / skyol), each with du gsol, 'I pray that you'. zhing mchog lnga, 'the five supreme realms', the realms of the five buddhas (006); ru, 'to', after a vowel, as in sa ru.

sentences.w: དེ་ལྟར་དུ་ སྨོན་ལམ་ བཏབ་པས༔ རང་སྣང་དུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ ནས་ གཉིས་སུ་ མེད་པར་ ཐིམ་ ནས་ སངས་རྒྱའོ༔
sentences.l: Thus prayer made-because: as-self-appearance face-knowing, then, two-as not-being-way dissolving, then, buddha-becomes.
sentences.i: When the prayer is made in this way, one recognises them as one's own appearance, dissolves into them without duality, and becomes a buddha.
sentences.n: This sentence and the next two say what the prayer does for three kinds of people. The other recension begins this one with rab, 'the best', so that the three are named in turn (the best, the middling, the lowest); the print has no rab, and the first sentence speaks of anyone. gnyis su med par, 'without being two', non-dually; the other recension has gnyis med du. sangs rgya'o, 'becomes a buddha', with -'o closing the sentence; the other recension has sangs rgyas so. The form without -s is kept as printed.

sentences.w: འབྲིང་ མོས་གུས་ དྲག་པོས་ རང་ངོ་ ཤེས་ ནས་ གྲོལ་བ་ ཐོབ་བོ༔
sentences.l: The-middling, devotion-respect fierce-by own-face knowing, then, liberation obtain.
sentences.i: Those of middling ability recognise their own nature through fierce devotion and are freed.
sentences.n: 'bring, 'middling': those of middling ability, as the rnal 'byor 'bring, 'middling yogins', of the pilot's opening verse. rang ngo shes, 'to know one's own face', recognition of one's own nature, as in the pilot. grol ba thob bo, 'attain liberation', with -bo closing the sentence after -b.

sentences.w: ཐམས་ཅད་ ཀྱང་ སྨོན་ལམ་ རྣམ་པར་ དག་པའི་ མཐུས་ རིགས་དྲུག་ གི་ མངལ་ གྱི་ སྒོ་ བཀག་ སྟེ༔ ཡེ་ཤེས་ བཞི་ སྦྱོར་ གྱི་ དོན་ རྟོགས་ ནས༔ རྡོ་རྗེ་སེམས་དཔའི་ ཁོང་སེང་ གི་ ལམ་ ལ་ སངས་རྒྱས་པར་ འགྱུར་རོ༔
sentences.l: All also, prayer completely pure's power-by, six-kinds' womb's door blocked, and; wisdoms four joined's meaning realised, then; Vajrasattva's inner-hollow's path on buddha become.
sentences.i: And all of them, through the power of the wholly pure prayer, close the door of the womb into the six kinds of beings, realise the meaning of the four wisdoms joined, and become buddhas on the path of the inner hollow of Vajrasattva.
sentences.n: thams cad kyang, 'all, every one, too'. Here the other recension has tha mas kyang, 'even the lowest', the third of the three kinds after 'the best' and 'the middling', and its reading fits the run of the three better. The print's letters are clear and its words give sense, so they are followed and translated; that they stand for tha mas is possible, not sure. mthus, 'by the power' (mthu, 'power', with -s). mngal gyi sgo, 'the door of the womb', the way into a new birth; the other recension has skye sgo, 'the door of birth'. bkag, the past stem of 'gog, 'to block' (005). rtogs, 'to realise'. khong seng is here in its usual spelling, where the print had khong gseng above.

sentences.w: ཡང་ དེ་ལྟར་དུ་ ཞི་བ་ ལ་ གསལ་བར་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པས་ ཤས་ཆེ་བ་ གཅིག་ ངོ་ འཕྲོད་ དེ་ གྲོལ་བ་ མང་དུ་ འབྱུང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Again, thus, peaceful-ones on clearly face-introduced-because: majority, one, face meeting, and: freed many-in occur.
sentences.i: Again, when the peaceful deities are pointed out clearly in this way, most recognise them, and many are freed.
sentences.n: zhi ba, 'the peaceful ones': the deities of the days so far, as against the wrathful ones (khro bo) still to come. la, 'with regard to'. gsal bar, 'clearly'; the other recension has gsar bar, 'newly'. shas che ba, 'the greater part' (shas, 'part, share'; che ba, 'great'); gcig, 'one', where the other recension has 'gro ba shas che ba zhig, 'a greater part of beings'. ngo 'phrod de, 'recognition comes, and', as in 006. mang du 'byung, 'occur in great number'.

sentences.w: ཐ་མའི་ ཡང་ ཐ་མ་ མི་ཡུལ་དུ་ ཆོས་ ཀྱི་ བག་ཆགས་ ཡེ་ནས་ མེད་པའི་ སྡིག་ཅན་ དང་༔ དམ་ཉམས་ ལ་སོགས་པ་ འགའ་ ཞིག་ ལས་ ཀྱིས་ འཁྲུལ་ ནས༔ ངོ་སྤྲད་ ཀྱང་ མི་ འཕྲོད་པར་ མར་ ལ་ འཁྱམས་དུ་ འོང་བས༔
sentences.l: The-lowest's even lowest, human-world-in dharma's habitual-tendencies not-at-all without's sinners and, commitment-broken etc., some, karma-by deluded, then; face-introduced though, not meeting-way, downward wandering come-because:
sentences.i: But some, the lowest of the low, are deluded by their karma: wrongdoers who in the human world had no tendency toward the teaching at all, those who broke their commitments, and the like. Though they are pointed out, they do not recognise, and they come wandering on downward.
sentences.n: tha ma'i yang tha ma, 'the lowest even of the lowest'. The print writes the second tha ma as one syllable (ཐམ), a contraction written out here. chos kyi bag chags, 'habitual tendencies of the dharma': the traces that practice in former lives leaves in the mind. ye nas med pa, 'not at all', as in the pilot. sdig can, 'one who has sin, a wrongdoer'. dam nyams, 'one whose commitment (dam tshig) is broken', the vows of tantric practice. la sogs pa, 'and the like'. 'ga' zhig, 'some'. ngo sprad kyang mi 'phrod par, 'though pointed out, without recognition coming'. mar la, 'downward, on', as in 006. 'khyams du 'ong, 'come wandering', has du where the rule gives su after -s, as the other recension also writes. 'ong bas runs on into the seventh day.

sentences.w: ཞག་ བདུན་པ་ ལ་ དག་བ་ མཁའ་སྤྱོད་ ཀྱི་ ཞིང་ ནས་ རིག་འཛིན་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ རྣམས་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོང་བས༔
sentences.l: Day seventh on, pure Sky-Going's realm from, knowledge-holders' deity-host (plural) meeting for come-because:
sentences.i: On the seventh day the hosts of the knowledge-holder deities come to meet them from the pure realm of the Sky-Goers,
sentences.n: zhag bdun pa, 'the seventh day'. The print writes pa la as one syllable (པལ), a contraction written out here, as the same words stand a few lines below. dag ba is the print's spelling of dag pa, 'pure'. mkha' spyod, 'sky-going' (mkha', 'sky'; spyod, 'to move, to enjoy'; Sanskrit khecara): the realm of the beings who move in space. rig 'dzin, 'knowledge-holder' (rig pa, 'knowledge'; 'dzin, 'to hold'; Sanskrit vidyādhara), a master of tantric knowledge. The -gs of tshogs is cut as one sign with s under g (ཚོགྶ), written out here. The other recension has zhing khams nas, 'from the realm'.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ ཉོན་མོངས་པ་ གཏི་མུག་ ལས་ གྲུབ་པའི་ དུད་འགྲོའི་ འོད་ལམ་ ཀྱང་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, affliction delusion from formed's animals' light-path also meeting for comes.
sentences.i: and at that time the light-path of the animals, formed from the affliction of delusion, also comes to meet them.
sentences.n: nyon mongs pa, 'affliction' (Sanskrit kleśa), the name for the poisons of the mind; gti mug, 'delusion', the poison of the first day. las grub pa'i, 'formed from', as in 006. The other recension has 'od lam gyis kyang, with -gyis marking the light-path as the one that comes; the sense is the same.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ རང་ ངོ་སྤྲད་པ་ ནི༔ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ བོས་ ལ་ འདི་སྐད་དོ༔ ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ ཉོན་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, self(?) face-introduction, as-for: the dead-one's by-name called, and, these-words: O child-of-noble-family! Not distracted-way listen!
sentences.i: To point this out at that time, call the dead person by name and say this: O child of noble family, listen without distraction.
sentences.n: The formula of the days before (006). rang, 'self', stands before ngo sprad pa here, where the other recension has yang, 'again'. It may say that the dead person is pointed out to himself, as rang ngo, 'one's own face', is known in rang ngo shes; the sense is uncertain, and `i` leaves the word out. bos, the past and imperative stem of 'bod, 'to call', as in 006; the other recension has 'bod.

sentences.w: ཞག་ བདུན་པ་ ལ་ བག་ཆགས་ དབྱིངས་སུ་ དག་པའི་ འོད་ ལྔ་ ཁྲ་བོ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ་༔
sentences.l: Day seventh on, habitual-tendencies in-the-expanse purified's lights five, multicoloured, dawning come.
sentences.i: On the seventh day the five lights of the habitual tendencies purified in the expanse will dawn in many colours.
sentences.n: bag chags dbyings su dag pa, 'habitual tendencies purified in the expanse': the traces of past action cleansed into the space of reality. 'od lnga, 'the five lights'; khra bo, 'multicoloured, variegated'. The other recension has 'od khra bo, without lnga, and shar du for 'char du.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ མཁའ་སྤྱོད་ ཀྱི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་སུ༔ རིག་འཛིན་ གྱི་ ལྷ་ཚོགས་ བསུ་བ་ ལ་ འོང་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, Sky-Going's realm-in, knowledge-holders' deity-host meeting for come, and:
sentences.i: At that time, in the realm of the Sky-Goers, the hosts of the knowledge-holder deities come to meet you:
sentences.n: zhing khams su, 'in the realm', where the sentence above had zhing nas, 'from the realm'; the other recension has dag pa mkha' spyod kyi zhing khams nas, 'from the pure realm of the Sky-Goers', here too. In the print the meeting takes place in that realm. 'ong ste runs on into the description of the first of them.

sentences.w: འཇའ་ དང་ འོད་དུ་ འཐིབ་པའི་ དབུས་སུ༔ རྣམ་པར་ སྨིན་པའི་ རིག་འཛིན་ བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ པདྨ་གར་གྱི་དབང་ཕྱུག་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ༔ སྐུ་མདོག་ འོད་ ལྔའི་ མདངས་ དང་ ལྡན་པ༔ ཡུམ་ མཁའ་འགྲོ་མ་ དམར་མོ་ སྐུ་ ལ་ འཁྲིལ་བ༔ གྲི་གུག་ དང་ ཐོད་ཁྲག་ འཛིན་ ཅིང་༔ བལྟ་སྟངས་ ཀྱི་ ཕྱག་རྒྱ་ ནམ་མཁའ་ ལ་ མཛད་པ་ ཅིག་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Rainbow and light-as thick's centre-in, ripening's knowledge-holder unsurpassed, Lotus Dance's Lord so-called, body-colour lights five's radiance with endowed, mother sky-goer-woman red body to embracing, curved-knife and skull-blood holding, and, gazing-manner's seal sky-to making, one, dawning comes.
sentences.i: In the midst of a dense mass of rainbow and light there dawns the unsurpassed knowledge-holder of full ripening, called Lord of the Lotus Dance, his body glowing with the radiance of the five lights, his consort, a red ḍākinī, embracing him; he holds a curved knife and a skull full of blood, and makes the gesture of gazing toward the sky.
sentences.n: 'thib pa, 'to gather thick', as clouds do; the other recension has 'ja' dang 'od du thim pa'i dkyil 'khor gyi dbus su, 'in the centre of a maṇḍala dissolving into rainbow and light'. rnam par smin pa'i rig 'dzin, 'the knowledge-holder of full ripening' (rnam par smin pa, 'fully ripened'): he stands in the centre; the next part names the knowledge-holders of the four directions. bla na med pa, 'with none above, unsurpassed'. Padma gar gyi dbang phyug, 'Lord of the Lotus Dance' (padma, 'lotus'; gar, 'dance'; dbang phyug, 'lord'). sku mdog, 'body colour', the respectful word. mkha' 'gro ma, 'she who goes in the sky' (Sanskrit ḍākinī); the print writes mkha' 'gro with one ' for both syllables (མཁའགྲོ), a contraction written out here. 'khril ba, 'winding about, embracing'. gri gug, 'curved knife'; thod khrag, 'skull and blood', a skull cup full of blood. 'dzin cing, 'holding, and'; the other recension has gri gug dang thod khrag gi gar mdzad cing, 'dancing with the curved knife and the skull of blood'. blta stangs, 'manner of looking, gaze' (blta, 'to look'; stangs, 'manner'; the other recension lta stangs); phyag rgya, 'gesture'; mdzad pa, the respectful 'make'. cig, 'one', makes it 'a knowledge-holder'. The part ends here, in the middle of p. 72.
